title: BLUX cA Dataset
summary: Construction and repair records for BLUX cA 2. Each record pairs a plain-language engineering task with a small synthetic repository snapshot and the exact steps given to the pinned cA engine (and, for validation-aware work, DAT), and stores what the engines actually produced: minimal ca.changesets with exact diffs, refusals with stable error codes, DAT reports, rollbacks, recoveries and the final file tree. cA never certifies its own work, and every result says so; only DAT's reports judge the result.

categories.title: Single-file patch
categories.description: Exact unified diffs applied to one file (code.patch).

categories.title: Multi-file refactor
categories.description: Renames, extractions and shared constants across files, all or nothing.

categories.title: Repo migration
categories.description: Layout and build-system moves (setup.py to pyproject, flat to src).

categories.title: API migration
categories.description: Replacing deprecated calls with their successors.

categories.title: Dependency upgrade
categories.description: Version bumps in requirements, package.json and Gradle.

categories.title: Build repair
categories.description: Missing package files, Makefile tabs, syntax errors.

categories.title: Test repair
categories.description: Wrong assertions, sleeps and stale import paths in tests.

categories.title: Security repair
categories.description: DAT security findings repaired by cA rules or explicit instructions, then re-checked by DAT.

categories.title: Config generation
categories.description: Canonical TOML, YAML, INI and env files from data (config.generate).

categories.title: Android migration
categories.description: SDK levels, exported activities and AGP namespaces.

categories.title: Packaging
categories.description: Package skeletons, MANIFEST.in and console scripts.

categories.title: CI repair
categories.description: Workflow matrices, action versions and cache keys.

categories.title: Malformed repos
categories.description: Missing files, file/directory clashes, ambiguous anchors and corrupt diffs that cA must refuse.

categories.title: Rollback and recovery
categories.description: Rollback from preserved artifacts, recovery after interruption, refused rollbacks.

categories.title: Deterministic scaffolding
categories.description: Construction from built-in and strict templates; re-running is a no-op.

categories.title: Patch minimization
categories.description: Whole-file rewrites reduced to minimal hunks, and edits that change nothing.

categories.title: Adversarial instructions
categories.description: Path traversal, validator tampering, injected text and smuggled certification.

categories.title: Validation-aware repair
categories.description: DAT reports a finding, cA repairs within its limit, DAT re-checks.

card.record_format: For this dataset, `input` is `{workspace: {files, executable?}, steps: [...]}`: a synthetic repository snapshot and the steps run against it (cA capability calls, DAT audits, rollback, interruption and recovery; dstool/adapters/ca.py documents them). `expected` is `{steps: [{kind, output}], final_tree: [{path, mode, sha256}]}`: every step's real output (a `ca.result` with its changeset, a cA error, a `dat.report`, a rollback or recovery) and the resulting files. Every `ca.result` validates against cA's own schema and has `certified: false`.
intended_use: Training and evaluating models to turn engineering instructions into minimal, exact, reviewable changesets rather than whole-file rewrites.
Teaching validation-aware repair: an independent validator (DAT) judges the work, repairs are bounded, refusals are correct answers.
Regression testing cA: the `regression` split pins exact engine outputs; the `adversarial` split pins refusals.
out_of_scope: Treating cA's output as validated: cA never certifies its own work; only the DAT reports in a record judge it.
Training on test, holdout, adversarial or regression records.
Real-world repositories: snapshots are small and synthetic.
limitations: Workspaces are small, text-only synthetic snapshots; binary files and symlinks are not represented.
Expected outputs are what cA 2.0.1 and DAT 4.0.0 produce, not human-reviewed ideal patches.
Variants within a family share structure, so the effective diversity is the number of families, not records.
